summary.headline: JSW Dulux Q4 FY26 revenue rose 6.2% on 23% blended volume growth, with price and mix cuts holding back realisations and EBITDA margin near 14.4%.
summary.overview: Management reported a record 23% blended volume growth across decorative and industrial paints, with revenue up 6.2%, the gap driven mainly by price and mix after premium price corrections from September-October 2025. Like-for-like EBITDA grew about 2% and PBT declined slightly, while the EBITDA margin was stated at around 14.4%. Management said raw material inflation since March 2026 has forced a price increase of about 9.7% through mid-May, with an estimated further 3-4% needed. The company also booked INR64.8 crore from the final real estate sale and proposed a final dividend of INR50 per share.

financial_highlights.change: Record, per management; decorative and industrial both grew strongly
YoY; one of strongest in last 4 quarters
Largely protected vs prior year per CFO
Last of real estate sale, completed March 2026

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Very strong volume growth amid competition; premium growth good, retail and semi-urban grew faster; Dulux Velvet Touch luxury finishes launched; mass and economy push increasing. Decorative is about 20% direct (projects) and 80% distributor-led, with roughly 75% of total via distributors.

segments.name: Industrial (Automotive & Specialty, Marine & Protective, Coil)
segments.commentary: Growth across all three verticals; mid-market automotive refinish under pressure; Porsche refinish tie-up announced; marine and protective had one of its highest revenue months in March; coil won marquee projects including Navi Mumbai Airport. Industrial capacity utilisation cited at 70-80%.

guidance_outlook: Management targets double-digit volume growth going forward, with the gap between volume and revenue expected to narrow over a couple of quarters.
Further price increase of about 3-4% needed industry-wide to offset RMC inflation of 24-25% (raw materials about 55% of RMC; implied about 13.5% need), per management estimate.
Price correction drag of about 1.5-2% expected to continue into the coming quarter; mix and price effects expected to neutralise by August-September.
FY27 margins may compress for about a quarter if elevated crude and raw material levels persist, though management sees no structural issue.
Integrated SAP and systems work planned around post-Diwali, towards end of calendar 2026; Mumbai HQ shift ongoing.
Dealer integration: projects business integrated; combined JSW Dulux and JSW Paints sales teams in 7 metros from later in May; retail integration only planned for early FY28 (early calendar 2027).
capex_capacity: Current decorative paint capacity utilisation stated at 55-60%.
Industrial capacity utilisation stated at up to 70-80% after additional capacity was added.

Cross-manufacturing being piloted: JSW Paints (earlier made only at Vijayanagar) to be made across plants; some southern-state products to move from Hyderabad and Thane to Vijayanagar; first trial batches produced.
Management said capex will be invested in capacity expansion and localisation; no specific amount or timeline disclosed.
demand_pricing: Blended volume growth of 23% partly reflected dealer pre-buying ahead of price increases, estimated at a week to 10 days; management said offtake tracked in line with sell-in.
Price increases of about 9.7% taken through mid-May 2026 (gross, before price-correction adjustments).
Premium contribution in Dulux at mid-40s percent vs about 22% for the industry; management said premium price premiums were cut from 7-9% and mid-market is now almost at parity with Berger.
Competition described as very intense; some competitors operating higher discounts; industry aggression expected for coming quarters.
Dealer and channel pushback after strategic review announcement in 2025 (warranty concerns) said to be behind the company.
Management aims to become a strong number 3 in decorative from number 4 (blended 8% market share target referenced; decorative progress described as a longer journey).

qa_highlights.question: Is cultural, dealer and systems integration complete, and has it hurt margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Culture integration early but going well; HQ moved to Mumbai. Only projects dealer integration done; retail integration planned for early next year. HR integrated. SAP integration planned around post-Diwali.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company over-indexed on premium pricing and at parity with Berger?
qa_highlights.answer: Some premium brands still carry about 2% desired premium; mid-market almost at par with Berger, though some competitors discount more.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 23% volume growth driven by channel fill or pre-buying, and what is FY27 volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth is blended and secular; some dealer pre-buy in March; offtake similar. Management targets double-digit volume growth over the long term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the effective price hike after price cuts and trade spend changes?
qa_highlights.answer: The 9.7% increase is gross; price correction impact of about 1.5-2% in the quarter continues into next quarter, to be absorbed by the price increase.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Decorative utilisation 55-60%, industrial up to 70-80%; cross-manufacturing underway; capacity expansion and localisation on the agenda, no figures given.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 outlook given oil and war-related uncertainty?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is scenario planning; elevated levels could compress margins for about a quarter, but structural demand is intact.

risks_watch: Raw material and crude-linked cost inflation (RMC inflation 24-25%); further pricing needed; margin compression risk for about a quarter.
Price correction and mix drag of 1.5-2% over the next quarter; volume-revenue gap to narrow.
Intense competition and discounting from peers; possible dealer destocking as price cuts and inventory levels differ across players.
Integration risk: retail dealer integration deferred; SAP and systems migration around end-2026.
Whether Q4 volume partly reflected March pre-buying, so Q1 FY27 sell-in may soften.
Auto OEM entry and decorative market-share gains still unproven; management timeline is towards the last quarter of FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume momentum and market-share ambitions, but cautious on margins and FY27 given raw material and geopolitical uncertainty. Management repeatedly deferred specifics (capex amounts, pricing bridge, margin guidance) and gave answers that were partly qualitative.
key_quotes: We've had a record volume growth of 23%, both on the decorative and industrial verticals.
So there's still about a 3% to 4% pricing from an industry perspective that we need to take, right?
And that's something that consumers are always aware of.
We are gaining at the cost of suppliers.

growth.why: Management targets double-digit volume growth in FY27 and a move from number 4 to strong number 3 in decorative, backed by a 9.7% price increase taken and cross-manufacturing trials, but no specific capacity additions, orders or amounts were disclosed, and decorative utilisation is only 55-60%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects margin compression for about a quarter if raw material inflation persists, with a further 3-4% price increase needed to offset RMC inflation of 24-25%; mix and price are expected to neutralise only by August-September.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Decorative utilisation is only 55-60% (growth_read util 57.5%), so there is spare decorative capacity; industrial at 70-80% got capacity added already, and no new plant, line or amount was disclosed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management is targeting double-digit volume growth in FY27 after 23% blended growth in Q4, backed by secular demand and share gains, though part of Q4 was dealer pre-buying (about a week to 10 days) so Q1 FY27 sell-in may soften.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said capex will go into capacity expansion and localisation, but gave no amount or timeline, and decorative utilisation of 55-60% gives little pressure to commit; industrial at 70-80% is the only tight spot.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management has only given a double-digit volume target and a share-gain ambition, with no numeric revenue or margin guidance to raise, and it flagged intense competition and discounting from peers.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged FY27 margin compression for about a quarter if crude and raw material stay elevated (RMC inflation 24-25%), and the 1.5-2% price correction drag continues into next quarter, though management says no structural issue.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Dulux Velvet Touch luxury finishes already launched and a Porsche refinish tie-up announced, but no further product pipeline or dates were disclosed.

rows.label: Further 3-4% industry price increase to offset RMC inflation
rows.why: Management has taken 9.7% gross price increase through mid-May 2026 and estimates a further 3-4% is needed against RMC inflation of 24-25% (raw materials about 55% of RMC, implied about 13.5% need).

rows.label: Cross-manufacturing of JSW Paints across plants
rows.why: Trial batches have been produced and some southern-state products are to move from Hyderabad and Thane to Vijayanagar, but no cost savings or timeline were quantified.

rows.label: Industrial coil marquee wins (Navi Mumbai Airport)
rows.why: Coil division won marquee projects including Navi Mumbai Airport and marine/protective had one of its highest revenue months in March, though no order value was disclosed.

tone.note: Management was confident on 23% volume momentum, share-gain ambition and integration progress, but cautious on margins, FY27 and raw material costs, and repeatedly deferred capex amounts, pricing bridge and margin guidance, which analysts pushed on.
